title: Modules: Scope, Inputs, Outputs and Composition

header.html: 5b Describe variable scope within modules; 5c Use modules in configuration
the official Terraform Associate (004) exam content list

html:
1Scope: modules are isolated

A module is its own scope. Its variables, locals and resources are private to it. The only ways data crosses the boundary are:

Direction Mechanism
Parent to child Input variables: arguments in the module block
Child to parent Output values: read as module.NAME.OUTPUT

The parent cannot read a child's resources, locals or variables directly, and the child cannot read the parent's.

# modules/network/variables.tf
variable "cidr_block" {
  type = string
}

# modules/network/outputs.tf
output "vpc_id" {
  value = aws_vpc.main.id
}

# root main.tf
module "network" {
  source     = "./modules/network"
  cidr_block = "10.0.0.0/16"
}

resource "aws_subnet" "app" {
  vpc_id     = module.network.vpc_id
  cidr_block = "10.0.1.0/24"
}
Exam tip

. A module only sees what is passed in as variables, and the parent only sees what the module exposes as outputs. Reference a child output as module.NAME.OUTPUT_NAME.

2Using a module in configuration

Step What to do
Call it A module "name" block with source
Pass inputs Arguments that match the module's variables; required variables must be set
Run terraform init Download the module (and re-run after adding or changing it)
Use outputs module.name.output elsewhere

Meta-arguments on a module block: count, for_each, depends_on, providers, version, source.

module "web" {
  source   = "./modules/web"
  for_each = toset(["a", "b"])
  name     = each.key
}

3Providers and modules

Rule Detail
Inheritance A child module uses the provider configurations of its parent by default
Explicit passing The providers argument passes a configuration (for example an aliased provider) to a child
Do not put provider blocks in reusable modules Let the caller configure providers; a module declares required_providers only 
module "backup" {
  source = "./modules/backup"
  providers = {
    aws = aws.west
  }
}

4Module composition and structure

Practice Meaning
Standard structure main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, and a README.md
Small, focused modules One purpose each (network, database, compute)
Compose, do not nest deeply The root module combines modules; pass outputs of one as inputs to another
Sensible inputs Few, well-typed variables with defaults and descriptions
Exam tip

. Compose modules in the root and connect them with outputs and inputs. Avoid hard-coded provider blocks inside a reusable module.

Exam tip

. Nothing crosses a module boundary except inputs and outputs. If a value is not an output, the parent cannot see it.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1How does a parent module read a value from a child module?

  • ADirectly from the child's resource
  • BThrough a local value of the child module
  • CThrough the child's variable
  • DThrough an output value of the child
Show the answer

Answer: D. Only outputs cross the module boundary toward the parent.

S2How is the output vpc_id of a module called network referenced?

  • Amodule.network.vpc_id
  • Bnetwork.vpc_id
  • Coutput.network.vpc_id
  • Dvar.network.vpc_id
Show the answer

Answer: A. Module outputs are referenced as module.NAME.OUTPUT.

S3How does a parent give a value to a module?

  • ABy setting an argument that matches an input variable
  • BBy declaring a local value in the child
  • CBy editing the child's state file
  • DBy using a data block in the child
Show the answer

Answer: A. Arguments in the module block become the values of the module's input variables.

S4A required input variable of a module has no value in the module block and no default. What happens on plan?

  • ATerraform reports an error or asks for the value
  • BTerraform uses an empty value
  • CTerraform copies the value from the parent
  • DTerraform uses the last known value
Show the answer

Answer: A. A required variable must be set, so Terraform reports it or asks for it.

S5A reusable module must create resources in a second region chosen by the caller. What should the caller use?

  • AA separate state file for the child
  • BA provider block inside the module
  • CA data block in the root
  • DThe providers argument to pass an aliased provider
Show the answer

Answer: D. The providers argument passes a provider configuration, such as an alias, to the child module.

S6After adding a new module block, which command must be run before plan?

  • Aterraform fmt
  • Bterraform init
  • Cterraform destroy
  • Dterraform output
Show the answer

Answer: B. terraform init downloads the new module.

5.2 Recall questions

R1How does data enter a module?

Show the answer

Through input variables.

R2How does data leave a module?

Show the answer

Through outputs.

R3How is a module output referenced?

Show the answer

module.NAME.OUTPUT.

R4Which argument passes an aliased provider?

Show the answer

providers.

R5What files form the standard module structure?

Show the answer

main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf and a README.

R6Can a parent read a child's local value?

Show the answer

No.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Scope module is isolated; inputs in, outputs out
Use module block, source, inputs, init, module.NAME.OUTPUT
Meta-arguments count, for_each, depends_on, providers, version
Providers inherited by default; providers argument to pass aliases; no provider blocks in reusable modules
Structure main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, README; small, composed modules
